title: Two finite cohomological inductions for an exact bifunctor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with derived categories and their standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category, $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$ a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], and $B:D(\mathcal A)\times D(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal T$ a bifunctor exact in each variable (preserving shifts and distinguished triangles in that variable). Let $\mathcal A_0,\mathcal B_0$ be classes of objects. Assume $B(F[0],G[0])\in\mathcal S$ for all $F\in\mathcal A_0,G\in\mathcal B_0$. Then $B(K,M)\in\mathcal S$ for all bounded $K,M$ with $H^q(K)\in\mathcal A_0$ and $H^q(M)\in\mathcal B_0$ for every $q$ for which the respective cohomology is nonzero. The zero objects and arbitrary finite cohomological intervals are included.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), applied successively in each variable

proof.text: An exact functor $G:D(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal T$ is additive. It preserves zero: $\mathrm{id}_{G(0)}=G(\mathrm{id}_0)=G(0)=0$. Set $Q_G(L)\iff G(L)\in\mathcal S$. Functors preserve isomorphisms; the shift comparisons and image distinguished triangles, together with strict fullness of $\mathcal S$, show that $Q_G$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts and extensions. No closure assumption on the original classes is used.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), finite truncation induction in each variable; abstract tower: BBD 1.3.3-1.3.6, 1.3.13

proof.text: Fix $F\in\mathcal A_0$ and $G=B(F[0],-)$. Choose $c\in\mathbf Z$, $n\in\mathbf N$ with $M\in D(\mathcal B)^{\ge c}\cap D(\mathcal B)^{\le c+n-1}$. Apply lem-sfb-bounded-postnikov-extension-generation to the standard t-structure and $M$. Its tower has $L_0\cong0$, $L_n\cong M$ and factor $H^r(M)[0][-r]$ at $r=c+j$. If $H^r(M)=0$, its degree-zero image under $G$ is zero. Otherwise $h_{MB}$ and the pair hypothesis give $G(H^r(M)[0])\in\mathcal S$. Shift closure and exactness give $Q_G$ on every factor. Induct on $j=0,\ldots,n$: the base is $Q_G(L_0)$; the tower triangle and extension closure give $Q_G(L_{j+1})$ from $Q_G(L_j)$. The endpoint isomorphism gives $B(F[0],M)\in\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), finite truncation induction in each variable; abstract tower: BBD 1.3.3-1.3.6, 1.3.13

proof.text: Fix $M$ and $G=B(-,M)$, and choose $a\in\mathbf Z$, $m\in\mathbf N$ with $K\in D(\mathcal A)^{\ge a}\cap D(\mathcal A)^{\le a+m-1}$. Apply lem-sfb-bounded-postnikov-extension-generation to $K$. For each tower factor $H^q(K)[0][-q]$, zero cohomology gives a zero image; otherwise $h_{KA}$ puts $H^q(K)$ in $\mathcal A_0$, and step 2 gives $G(H^q(K)[0])\in\mathcal S$. Shift closure gives $Q_G$ on the factor. Starting from the zero endpoint, induction on the $m$ triangles gives $Q_G$ on every successive middle vertex by exactness and extension closure. Transport across the final isomorphism to obtain $B(K,M)\in\mathcal S$. Negative intervals, gaps, acyclic inputs and empty classes cause no change: only nonzero cohomology uses the class hypotheses.
